industry.key: P. Energy, commodities and metals mining
industry.why: Neutral, carried; the condition back to B (industry relative strength returning to B with oil holding) is not met: relative strength C (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; A prior), Brent near $90 (Goldman, Struyven, 22-Nov) from $111 to $115 at the October reads. The sector rows carry the view (Downstream A, Upstream B, Services B) and each is $5 from its $85 trigger, with Goldman's base case ($88 average in 2027, $78 by December 2027) going through it and Kofler (Jefferies, 21-Nov) fearing Iran escalation the other way. 18 Pool names. Back to B if relative strength returns to B with Brent holding above $85.

sector.key: P.3. Energy - services and engineering contractors
sector.why: Overweight, carried against the tape: relative strength D (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; B prior), the conditions for Neutral (Brent under $85, or relative strength F) not met. Held on Kepler Cheuvreux's structural read of 29-Oct (vessels booked 18 to 24 months) and on Kofler (Jefferies, 26-Nov): oil country tubular goods pricing up 30% year to date, October's 9% rise the largest in eighteen years, 20% earnings growth likely at Tenaris and Vallourec. No Pool name. Counter-case: the most operationally geared end of energy with oil down about $20 since October. To C if Brent is read under $85 or relative strength falls to F.

geography.why: Overweight, from Neutral, on the row's own written condition ('to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read'): Goldman's Sharon Bell (20-Nov) argues 'Domestic not Defensive' with 2027 growth of 1.4% above consensus and the FTSE 100 at a discount with a far higher free-cash-flow yield, James Moberly (23-Nov) has growth improving through 2027 as rates peak, Marshall (22-Nov) has gilts at 4.8% by end-2027, UK core inflation is flat at 2.8% (25-Nov), and Jefferies' Duncan Farr (26-Nov) reads the Financial Policy Committee ruling as favourable for bank cost of equity. 28 Pool stocks are UK-listed and now carry a country weight in Thematic Fit/Momentum; the book holds 16.47 points UK-listed (CVS Group, Fevertree, Hilton Food, Helios Towers). Counter-case: Bell's next two quarters are 'tough', the Bank of England's decision is still unread, Oppenheimer underweights Europe as a whole, and the UK Pool names are mostly global businesses. Back to C if the Bank of England's guidance is read hawkish or a UK consumer reading arrives falling.
